name: @macintacos/caret
description: A Claude Code plugin that replaces the terminal plan-approval prompt with a local web UI for inline review, annotation, and approval.

pinned.//: bun.lock is committed, so it is what pins every dependency exactly; a range above is the upgrade policy, not the resolved version. A bare version therefore means `bun update` must never move this one on its own, and these entries are the whole set. Everything else takes a range deliberately — zod and the TOML parser reading the config.toml trust boundary included: the lockfile already holds them, so a range costs no reproducibility and keeps them visible to an upgrade sweep. test/structure/exact-pin.test.ts fails on an exact pin with no reason, and on a reason that outlived its pin.
pinned.@pierre/diffs: Version-coupled to shiki through the resolve.alias block in ui/vite.config.ts, where an alias that stops matching grows the bundle by ~600 KB silently rather than failing anything. The pair moves as one reviewed bump, never on a sweep.
pinned.@pierre/trees: No stable release exists — the `latest` and `beta` dist-tags both point at the same prerelease. Exact rather than caret because a prerelease under a caret range is still a caret range: `^1.0.0-beta.6` expands to `>=1.0.0-beta.6 <2.0.0-0`, so a sweep would take a stable 1.0.0 the day it lands, and beta-to-stable is the jump that wants a human.

held.//: A dependency whose range deliberately stops below the current major, with the evidence for that and the condition that lifts it. Distinct from `pinned` above, which is about exact versions: an entry here names a range that is doing its job by excluding something. Unlike a pin, a held range is self-describing to `bun outdated` — it shows up as a major behind — so this block answers the question it raises rather than surfacing a decision nothing else would show.
held.typescript: NOT a hold on adoption — TypeScript 7 IS what type-checks this tree (EXC-1089). It arrives as the `@typescript/native` alias above; hk.pkl runs the backend program through node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc and the UI program through `svelte-check --tsgo`, and both were proved live against injected type errors rather than trusted because they exited 0. This range stops at ^6 because svelte-check requires BOTH majors installed: 4.7.5 hard-throws from bin/ts-version-check.js once `typescript` is major >= 7, and the recipe it throws is the arrangement used here verbatim — `typescript@~6 @typescript/native@npm:typescript@7`, plus --tsgo. Its README repeats it and dist/src/index.js resolves `@typescript/native` before `@typescript/native-preview`, so this is upstream's supported setup rather than a workaround. A second reason keeps 6.x honest even so: test/structure/e2e-conventions.test.ts and test/structure/tokenize-conventions.test.ts import the compiler API as a PARSING LIBRARY, and 7.x exports lib/version.cjs as `.` with the API behind ./unstable/* subpaths that offer no standalone parse (unstable/ast's createSourceFile is a factory over Statement[]; the only SourceFile producer is Program.getSourceFile). With 6.x installed those two files need no port, and `tsc` 7 type-checks them clean — the 50 errors EXC-1083 measured were never caret's code, only two files typed against a package whose `.` export had moved. What lifts this: a svelte-check release whose peerDependencies.typescript admits ^7 — but that clears only the first reason. Collapsing to a single `typescript@7` means dropping the alias, moving this range to ^7, AND porting those two suites off the compiler API in the same pass, or they break on `ts.ScriptTarget` being undefined. test/structure/typescript-arrangement.test.ts reds on exactly that widening, and also pins the tsc path, the --tsgo flag, and this entry's own existence, because losing any of them silently reverts the adoption. Full evidence: EXC-1089, and the trial in EXC-1083.
